# v1.1.0-dev.102: Docking, the way an IDE does it

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.101`.

Virtual Windows shipped last release as a container that held windows in
whatever arrangement you left them. This release makes docking mean what
it means in Visual Studio and Rider, and that changes something the last
release promised. The section on sizes says which.

## Drag a window onto a container and it shows you where it will go

Pick up any window by its title bar, drag it over a Virtual Window, and
guides appear: four edge targets and a shaded rectangle showing exactly
the shape the window is about to take. Let go on one and the window fills
that half of the pane you aimed at.

The shaded box is not an approximation. It is the same rectangle the drop
uses, worked out the same way, so what you see under the cursor is what
you get when you release.

Hold **Ctrl** while dragging and nothing docks, the way Ctrl suppresses
snapping in Visual Studio. Let go anywhere that is not a container and the
window just lands where you dropped it.

## Panes that meet have a bar you can drag

Two windows side by side in a container have a gap between them. That gap
is a splitter. Drag it and both windows resize together, live. Let go and
it is remembered with the profile.

## Docking now resizes your windows, which it did not before

Last release said that nothing you dock is ever altered, only moved. That
was true then and it is not true now. A pane decides how big a window is,
because that is what makes a drop land where the guide said it would.

So the size a window arrives with is remembered, and handed back the
moment you undock it, even if you resized it in between. Docking borrows a
size rather than replacing one.

Some windows will not take the size a pane gives them. An app with a
minimum size lands at its minimum and Windows reports the change as
successful either way. WLM checks afterwards and says so on the
container's own title bar rather than leaving you to wonder why one
window is sitting wrong.

## There are still no tabs, on purpose

Both IDEs stack windows into a tabbed group when you drop one in the
middle of a pane. WLM refuses that drop instead.

A tabbed group has to hide every window in it but the active one, and
hiding a window you did not ask to hide is the same kind of thing as
taking it over, which this feature does not do. Nothing docked is ever
reparented and nothing has its own title bar or styles touched. Every
member stays an ordinary window that WLM moves and sizes.

## A container appears the moment you make it

Create one on the Virtual Windows tab and it is on screen straight away,
so you can drag windows into it immediately. It belongs to the profile you
have open in the editor, and closes when you move on to editing another.

## It looks like a window now

A container is drawn from the same parts an ordinary window is, in both
the list and the visual editor, so it drags, resizes and moves between
monitors identically. The only things marking it out are a dashed frame
and a small badge with the number of windows inside it.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
